explanation: Administrative regions have been in the constitution since 1976 and have never existed. Creating them was a Socialist commitment carried into the 1995 campaign. The government this election produced turned that commitment into a law of regional delimitation and then into the referendum of 8 November 1998. Nobody else would have called it. The Social Democrats campaigned against, the referendum failed on both questions, and no government has proposed regionalisation since. This edge is `caused` rather than `enabled` because the ballot exists for one reason only, that this government decided to hold it.
